notes: A public download is not proof that commercial model training is permitted.
External labels must retain dataset provenance and must not be silently converted into native CrisisPulse reviews.
Weak or partially compatible labels must not be used in the final native CrisisPulse holdout.

datasets.source_name: Groundsource: A Global Dataset of Historical Flood Events

compatibility_mapping.source_label: reported past or ongoing flood event

evidence.supports: The public record describes one 667.1 MB Parquet file containing 2.6 million structured historical flood-event records.
The official DOI metadata identifies the dataset license as Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.
The primary manuscript documents only uuid, area_km2, start_date, end_date, and geometry in the released schema.
The project distinguishes reported flood events from warnings, policy discussion, and general risk.

notes: The CC BY 4.0 license permits reuse with attribution, but the file contains no article text, URL, title, publisher, or class-label column.
This is an event archive, not a four-class article-text dataset.
It may validate time-and-location matches for reported-flooding positives, but it cannot directly train the CrisisPulse article classifier.

datasets.source_name: Flood Event Extraction from News Media to Support Satellite-Based Flood Insurance

evidence.supports: The paper reports a Bangladesh news corpus and an expert-annotated binary flood-versus-not-flood subset.

notes: This is the closest located dataset to the CrisisPulse article-classification task.
Its not-flood class can mix flood warnings, heavy rain, policy discussion, and unrelated material.
A usable data file, article-text rights, and a training license have not yet been verified.

evidence.supports: The paper describes human-labeled social-media posts across disaster events and humanitarian categories.
The project page is the dataset access reference supplied by the authors.
The official terms limit use to humanitarian-computing research and impose confidentiality and deletion requirements.

notes: Social-media wording and humanitarian categories do not directly match news headlines or the four CrisisPulse classes.
The current terms are not suitable for commercial CrisisPulse product training.
A separately approved research experiment would still need to preserve the original social-media provenance.

datasets.label_type: multimodal crisis labels on social-media posts and images

evidence.supports: The project describes a labeled multimodal social-media crisis dataset.

notes: The medium, event coverage, and labels do not directly match the CrisisPulse article classifier.
Image and social-post experiments are outside the current training milestone.

datasets.source_name: Natural Disaster and Critical Event Detection from News

evidence.supports: The primary publication describes human annotation of agency news into flood and other concrete-event classes.

notes: The news medium and flood-event class are conceptually close to CrisisPulse.
No public corpus download or reusable dataset license was verified from the primary publication.
The non-flood classes still do not map cleanly to flood warning, heavy rain, and unrelated news.

datasets.label_type: crisis information-type and priority annotations on social-media posts

evidence.supports: The NIST publication describes annotated social-media posts for crisis events, information types, and priority.

notes: These annotations may inform a future urgency model but do not supply the current flood article labels.
Dataset access terms and any underlying platform-content restrictions must be reviewed separately.
